meaning: something that is very easy to do
example: The exam was a piece of cake because I had studied all week.
origin: Possibly from American slang of the early 1900s, where something easy was compared to an easy-to-eat slice of cake

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning, not the idiomatic one; the idiom has nothing to do with food.
The idiom describes something very easy, the opposite of dangerous.
The idiom says nothing about refusing; it is about how simple a task is.

explanation: 'Piece of cake' means something is very easy to do. It is informal and is used to describe tasks, tests, or problems that require little effort.
